reader.requirement: At --std 85, a Format 2 RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE clause that writes both FROM integer-2 and TO integer-3 must be refused unless integer-3 is strictly greater than integer-2 (equal and inverted bounds both refused), for every file the clause can describe (sequential, relative, indexed FD and the SD), with or without the DEPENDING phrase.

edition-consulted.switches: edition.DialectLevel >= Since; the SR5/1985-SR3 row has Since 85, so the row is screened at 85 exactly as at 2023 (only the Format 3 SR9 row is Since 2002)
diagnostic citation only: DialectLevel < 2002 prints 'ANSI §1985:VII.3.8.3 SR3' instead of 'ISO §2023:13.18.43.3 SR5'

reader.edition-search: Read RecordClauseRules.Screen end to end and Rule1985; the predicate (hi <= lo) has no edition test.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no (only the cited rule designation differs; the refusal is the same at 85 and 2023)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses are free-form sequential FDs with DEPENDING; relative, indexed, SD, no-DEPENDING and large-operand forms are not exercised by them (probed here)

citations.check: OK  §1985:VII.3.8.3 SR3  (3.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3

reader.notes: The one table row (Since 85) screens the strict inequality at every edition; at 85 the diagnostic cites the 1985 rule via Rule1985. The 1985 text prints the RECORD clause once (Sequential I-O VII.3.8) and the screen reaches every FD and SD. At --std 2023 the equal-bounds probe gives the same refusal citing §2023:13.18.43.3 SR5.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VII.3.8 whole (Formats 1-3, SR1-4, GR1-10) and RecordClauseRules.cs (Rules, AppliesAt, Render/CitationAt). The SR5 row is Since 85; the Format 3 row (SR9) is Since 2002, so SR3 does not overreach into Format 3, which 1985 leaves without an ordering rule. Probes at --std 85 (refute-1985-07/c1): f3eq.cob RECORD CONTAINS 5 TO 5 CHARACTERS -> RAN f3eq (Format 3, outside SR3, accepted); lz.cob FROM 0015 TO 015 -> COBOL2009 'FROM 15 TO 15 ... (ANSI §1985:VII.3.8.3 SR3)' (compared by value); ext.cob EXTERNAL FD FROM 15 TO 15 -> COBOL2009; nest.cob the FD in a contained program (1985 IPC nesting) FROM 15 TO 15 -> COBOL2009, so the screen reaches every program; odorun.cob FROM 6 TO 15 DEPENDING ON with an ODO record writes 8 and 6 bytes and reads them back '0008 2ABCDEXY' / '0006 0ABCDE', and WS-LEN 16 gives status 44 (GR10's last paragraph). cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VII.3.8.3 SR3  (3.8.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3'; 'OK  §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR10  (3.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR10'. No reading of 1985's SR3 found that the compiler fails.
